pages.text: A framework is a crystal of nodes and struts, mostly empty. On the $(item)Framework Assembler$() the linker sets the pore: it must fit the target molecule, and the solvent must be dried out slowly or the pores collapse. $(item)MOF Gas Sorbent$() fills a $(item)MOF Gas Storage Cell$(), which holds 256,000 mB of one gas - sixteen tanks' worth, because the framework holds gas on its inner surface (Langmuir). $(item)Silica Aerogel$() is ninety-nine parts air.

Clay digested in caustic soda gives $(item)Alumina$() (Bayer); electrolysed, $(item)Aluminium$() (Hall-Héroult). In the $(item)Quasicrystal Furnace$() an aluminium-copper-iron melt quenched at 10² to 10⁴ K/s, near 63% aluminium, freezes into a $(item)Quasicrystal Plate$(): order without repetition.
